Supply (CFO 'governor') is why we do not convert Q3's record wireline orders (more than double y/y) faster: the build stays below order growth. FY26 1,872. FY2027-29 growth = 1/3 x market growth (manufacturing test scales with units shipped) + 2/3 x customers' lab R&D growth. R&D growth = the customers' R&D-to-market elasticity x market growth: the wireline customer basket's R&D rose +36.0% y/y (src 56) while LightCounting's CY2026 market grows +120% (src 17), elasticity 0.36/1.20 = 0.30; on the market path (+76% 2027, LightCounting src 17; +30.6% 2028 and +27.1% 2029, src 51/17) R&D grows +22.8% / +9.2% / +8.1%. Within each year the quarters rise at one constant quarterly rate from the Q4 FY26 build so the FY totals hold (wireline has no stable seasonal pattern: it is a structural ramp). Capture = wireline / market: Q4 FY26 5.00%, FY27 4.12%, FY28 3.67%, FY29 3.30%. Europe: European Allies and Canada at 2.53% of GDP in 2026 vs the Hague 3.5% core-defence target by 2035 (NATO estimates via ICDS, published 2026-07-09, src 66); CEO (src 40): 'Sovereign investments in Europe is another tailwind for our defense business'.
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY26 379.5 built y/y on the same quarter's actual (330, Q4 FY25): organic +10% (CEO: ADG orders up double digits in all regions and backlog built in Q3; the DoD obligated ~$60B of reconciliation money in Aug-Sep on top of a record base budget, which reaches the primes and labs that buy KEYS test gear; the October CR month limits new starts, so organic growth stays at the low end of double-digit orders) plus +5pt from Spirent's PNT line, which was in the base for only two weeks of Q4 FY25 (closed 2025-10-15; 10-Q acquisition effect 5-7pt in 9M FY26). FY26 1,458. FY2027 +9% (organic; the CR to 2026-12-11 delays new starts in Q1, while the FY2026 record budget and the reconciliation obligations made in Aug-Sep convert to orders through FY27; Europe sovereign spending per CEO, src 40) -> 1,589; FY2028 +2.9% -> 1,635, FY2029 +3.9% -> 1,698: half US, half Europe/rest (judgment: KEYS does not split ADG by region; the CEO says growth is across all regions, src 18). US part: FY2028 flat in nominal terms (base discretionary held near the $1.1T FY2027 level while reconciliation money ends, src 64/65), FY2029 +2% (flat real with inflation at the Fed's 2% target, src 64). Europe part: +5.8% a year = the share path from 2.53% of GDP (2026) to 3.5% by 2035 (+3.7% a year, src 66) plus 2% inflation (ECB target). 0.5 x 0% + 0.5 x 5.8% = 2.9% (FY28); 0.5 x 2% + 0.5 x 5.8% = 3.9% (FY29). Quarters by the mean ADG quarter share of FY23-FY25 (25.2/24.4/24.1/26.3%; src 46-48). Alternatives: a full-year CR holds FY27 near +3%; a reconciliation-led year +12%; FY28-29 US-led (0% / +2%) or Europe-led (+5.8% / +5.8%).

drivers.label: CSG operating margin (segment = non-GAAP)
drivers.source: Actuals: Ex.99.1 segment results. Q2 FY26 includes the IEEPA tariff refund (+$38M CSG op income, -$34M revenue; 10-Q MD&A). CFO Neil Dougherty, Q3 FY26 prepared remarks (src 18): CSG gross margin 70.8%, op margin 34.0%; core 'operating margin incremental of 66 percent'; synergy realization 'will accelerate in Q4', 80-90% of the $100M run-rate exiting FY26. CFO on the call (src 40): FY27 'outperform our 40% leverage target, particularly given the synergy realization'; ~$40M realized in FY26, ~$50M more FY26 to FY27; 'upper 60s percent' gross margin sustainable; one-time tariff gains 'won't repeat'. CEO (src 40): Q4 mix toward production. Peer: VIAVI non-GAAP op margin 29.0% (Ex.99.1, src 41); CFO Ilan Daskal guides 29.3% +/- 30bp for Oct-Dec (VIAVI call, src 54; Zacks src 55). CFO (src 40): FY26 synergies 'close to $40 million', FY26 to FY27 'on the order of $50 million', 'close to 90% of that $100 million realized as we enter next fiscal year'.
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY26 35.9%: CSG op income 458 (Q3 actual) + incremental margin 56.8% on the +95.6 revenue the end-market build adds (CSG gross margin 70.8% less 2pt for the production tilt the CEO expects, less ~12% variable opex such as commissions and variable pay) + $5M synergy step (CFO: realization accelerates in Q4 toward an 80-90M run-rate exit) = 517.6 on 1,440.6. FY2027 35.7%: start from the H2 FY26 exit (Q3 + Q4 x 2 = 1,951 op income on 5,571 revenue; no tariff refund in H2) and add the CFO's 40% leverage target on the +603 revenue (he expects to outperform it, so 40% is the conservative end) plus ~$12M of the remaining synergies (100M program less the ~85M run-rate exiting FY26) -> 2,205 on 6,176. FY2028 36.1% and FY2029 36.4%: 40% incremental margin on each year's revenue growth (the company's long-term leverage target), no further synergies. Quarters within each year: each quarter's op income = the year margin on average quarterly revenue + 40% of that quarter's revenue above or below the average (fixed-cost absorption). Peak-cycle risk: these are above KEYS's 30.3% FY23 prior peak (proxy, src 15) and VIAVI's 29% (src 41); the mid-cycle leg (30% weight) and the downside case (-4pt) carry that risk.
